cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Investment in the Next Round
cards.instruction: Describe defeat, penalty, or a bad bargain as a deliberate investment in a larger future win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Selling our stall at a loss bought us information for the next one. I'll choose the new pitch after we've put that lesson on paper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which lesson? We just ran out of customers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely. I paid to discover what a hidden pitch earns. You can call it a failed stall; I call it research for one people can actually see.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The pitch by the entrance costs twice as much. We can't risk another blind purchase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll count the foot traffic there before I make an offer. Our loss has paid for a rule: no rent without visible customers. Bring the counts to me; the next stall has to earn back the first one too.

reason: Use B higher-price/risk objection to cause a concrete traffic check before A next decision; frame the real prior loss as deliberately purchased knowledge toward a larger recovery win.
